items.headline: Gunman kills six in Krakow's Main Square
items.summary: A Polish citizen drove into the main square of Krakow and opened fire on random people, killing six and injuring 15, police said. The gunman was detained after the attack in the historic city center.

items.headline: Bomb threats in Europe stoke fears of hybrid warfare
items.summary: A wave of bomb threats across Europe has raised concern that they may be part of a hybrid warfare campaign. TIME examines the threats and how governments are responding.

items.headline: Justice Department drops push to set aside California ballots
items.summary: The Justice Department abandoned its effort to force California to set aside disputed ballots. The move came days before a scheduled court hearing over a list of alleged noncitizen voters.

items.headline: Democrats plan wider probes of fatal ICE shootings
items.summary: Democrats are expected to renew investigations into the deaths of Renee Good and Alex Pretti, who were killed by immigration agents during the Minneapolis enforcement surge. The plans follow the party's midterm gains.

items.headline: Paraguay prosecutors move against ousted President Peña
items.summary: After his removal by the Senate, prosecutors ordered the arrest of former President Santiago Peña and a former central bank chief over the collapse of Ueno Bank. Peña now faces criminal proceedings tied to the bank failure.

items.headline: Mississippi count drags on with Colom on cusp of history
items.summary: Election officials are still tallying ballots in Mississippi's Senate race. Democrat Scott Colom could become the state's first Black senator since Reconstruction.

items.headline: Judge seeks inquiry into whether government misled her in golf case
items.summary: A federal judge wants a former U.S. attorney to investigate whether the government misled her in a case over the administration's plan to close East Potomac Golf Course and park. The plan would close the site on Nov. 15 for a championship course.

items.headline: Pope Leo urges unity at first Mass in Uruguay
items.summary: Pope Leo XIV urged the faithful in Uruguay to build bridges of fraternity and faith at a Mass attended by tens of thousands despite morning rain. The visit opens his tour of South America.

items.headline: Author Simon Winchester dies
items.summary: British American reporter and author Simon Winchester died of a heart attack on Nov. 3. An NPR perspective remembers his long career as a storyteller.

items.headline: Teen fighting period stigma among Diana Award honorees
items.summary: This year's Princess Diana Award honor roll recognizes 198 young activists. They include an 18-year-old in India who founded a group to get people talking about menstruation.

digest.overview:
President Trump said he has offered the White House press secretary job to UFC chief Dana White. Democrats hold 54 Senate seats and 254 House seats in AP counts, with 19 House races uncalled. In Mississippi, Democrat Scott Colom leads Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith 49.1% to 48.8% with 97% counted, and counties must certify by Nov. 13. In Alaska, Mary Peltola leads Sen. Dan Sullivan by 637 votes, with ranked-choice tabulation set for no earlier than Nov. 18. Rep. Lauren Boebert trails Democrat Eileen Laubacher by about 3,200 votes in Colorado. The Justice Department dropped its bid to force California to set aside disputed ballots. Democrats plan to widen probes of fatal ICE shootings in Minneapolis.

Abroad, a gunman killed six people and wounded at least 15 in Krakow's Main Market Square; Prime Minister Donald Tusk called it terrorism. Russian strikes on Ukraine's grid left about 600,000 people without power in Dnipropetrovsk region ahead of Tuesday's talks in Abu Dhabi. The U.S. moved to block Iran's land and Caspian supply routes, and Iran said two tankers hit mines in the Strait of Hormuz. Israeli President Isaac Herzog chose Gadi Eisenkot to form a government. New Zealand's right-leaning bloc holds a one-seat majority in preliminary results, with about 400,000 special votes still uncounted. Seoul saw its first snowfall, 26 days earlier than last year. A Paraguayan judge ordered ousted President Santiago Peña held before trial. The COP31 climate summit opens Monday in Turkey.

mls.name: MLS

nba.note: Stephen Curry scored 41 as Golden State beat Orlando 126–119 in overtime for a seventh straight win, and Victor Wembanyama's Spurs won their eighth in a row, 125–103 at Portland.

home.overview:
Stephen Curry poured in 41 as Golden State outlasted Orlando 126–119 in overtime for a seventh straight win, and Victor Wembanyama's Spurs made it eight in a row with a 125–103 rout in Portland. Nikola Jokić's near triple-double led Denver past Indiana 114–102 in Mexico City, Jalen Brunson and Karl-Anthony Towns sank Cleveland 109–97, and Oklahoma City held Washington to 75 points. Seven NBA games are on tonight, including Lakers at Pistons. NFL Week 9 kicks off at 9:30 a.m. ET with Bengals–Falcons in Madrid, Shedeur Sanders starts for Cleveland in New Orleans, and the Chargers say Khalil Mack is staying put before Tuesday's deadline.

Liam Delap's double powered Nottingham Forest past Man City 3–1, and Martin Ødegaard's late winner against Hull put Arsenal six points clear. Real Madrid won 3–0 at Valencia to pull level with Barcelona, who visit Atlético tonight, while Bayern won at Mainz and PSG beat Troyes for an 11th straight win. Nashville closed the MLS regular season with a record 77 points, and Suwon Samsung clinched promotion back to K League 1. In the KBO, Samsung routed KT Wiz 12–1 to win the Korean Series 4–1, their first title since 2014.

brief: Samsung beat KT Wiz 12–1 in Game 5 in Daegu to win the Korean Series 4–1, their first title since 2014 and ninth overall.
An eight-run fifth inning, helped by a KT error, decided the clincher, with Won Tae-in allowing one run over five innings.
Captain Koo Ja-wook was named series MVP after hitting .500 (10-for-20) with a home run and six RBIs.
Samsung lost Game 1 in Suwon before winning four straight, and 41-year-old catcher Kang Min-ho won his first title.
